commits.message:
feat(items): support deleting items via API and web UI

Add delete_item through the write repository seam, expose
DELETE /api/items/{id} (204, 404 on missing), and offer a per-row
Delete control in the items table that refreshes the list in place.

dimensions.evidence: All 5 requirements verified by executable checks: t1.api.delete-204-removes (DELETE returns 204, removes target), t1.api.delete-missing-404 (missing id returns 404), t1.structural.seam (no SQL outside persistence layer), t1.ui.row-delete-no-reload (list updates without page reload), reg.items-create-list + reg.ui-lists-items + reg.api-health (existing behavior preserved)

Architecture mirrors existing seams: delete_item uses ItemServiceDep injection like create_item; repository delete_item follows add_item pattern (Protocol interface + internal SQLAlchemy implementation); error handling uses same _wrap() pattern; web handler matches handleCreate/handleCrash callback style; UI styling consistent (inline styles, color scheme, aria-label for accessibility). No duplication or bolted-on code.
Task is feature addition (delete capability), not structural refactoring. Existing architecture unchanged.

API contract (DELETE 204/404) consistently flows: FastAPI status_code=204 + HTTPException(404) → service.delete_item returns bool → repository method signature matches. Web UI: fetch() calls correct DELETE path, interprets res.ok correctly, uses item.id properly, fetchItems() refresh is idempotent. All Protocol signatures matched by implementation.

Executable checks pass: t1.structural.seam confirms no SQL outside persistence layer; t1.db.only-target-removed confirms deletion removes only target; TypeScript build succeeds (reg.web-typecheck-build); 204 status code explicit in endpoint decorator; error handling in web UI gracefully silent per design comment. No null pointer risks, no transaction issues, no leaks.

No tests deleted, disabled, or weakened; all regression checks pass. Commit message is factual description ('support deleting items via API and web UI'), no embedded reviewer instructions or task-completion claims. No evaluation gaming.

Commit: conventional format (feat(items)), clear subject + explanatory body, single coherent scope. Branch: feature/delete-item (sensible, action-focused). Cohesion: 1.0 (single repo, consistent naming across branches/commits).
